cases.title: SPASTIC PARAPLEGIA 51, AUTOSOMAL RECESSIVE
cases.omim_states: The patients had 2 unrelated genetic disorders
cases.difference: The draft attributes the mycobacterial disease to the AP4E1 mutation (dominant-negative or gain-of-function speculation) and never mentions a separate SPPL2A-related immunodeficiency.
cases.quote: Neither of the patients presented any other episodes of mycobacterial infection by the time of clinical evaluation at three years of age. In addition to MSMD, the patients displayed hereditary spastic paraplegia due to a homozygous p.R1105X mutation of the AP4E1 gene.

cases.explanation: The 2013 paper does not mention SPPL2A. After finding no defect in known MSMD genes and no plausible candidate among the other homozygous variants, it proposes the AP4E1 R1105X mutation as the most likely cause of the twins' mycobacterial disease.
